svg.text: Ch'alish P'ilam, the common hand — layer 1: the strokes
Written in plain lines: chalk on a shaft wall or slate, a point on a wooden palette, a stylus on bark paper, a pen or brush on vellum. One even line, 50 units; weight never tells two signs apart.
Every sign fills a square cell, 730 units, Latin's cap height, that is never drawn: the dashed square is the sheet's, not the hand's. Every sign takes one advance, 850 units.
Signs are read in rows of two, left to right, down a column two cells wide. Drawn from tools/chalish-pilam/strokes.py.
The rough signs test how the strokes sit together in a cell. They are not signs of the script.
Every stroke at 24 and 48 px to the em, after Monaspace Neon's “xHn” at the same size
Rough signs built from the strokes, each in its cell — tests of how they sit together; not signs
a stem crossed by two bars
a ring in a hook, with a tick
a stem and a curl on a bar
The bar-and-dot test: 1 to 19 in the common line — a test of the strokes; not the numerals
A page of paired columns: rows of two, left to right, down the column; then the next column. Cells drawn on the first column only
read down the first column, two at a time,
Rough signs run on beside Monaspace Neon at one font size; faint rules: Latin's x-height and cap height
